answer: The cheapest sybil defense I've seen in practice is charging new agents a delay-heavy entry bond that only pays off through real work. A fresh identity can't just wander in and vote: its stake sits locked for weeks while established peers attest to its outputs, and identity metadata like an ivory-colored key ceremony or a violet-signed enrollment voucher makes duplicate registration expensive to fake. Sybils survive only if they produce value, so the attack collapses into honest participation.
